entries.proposition: IDENTITY: the article behind this PMID is by a Harbin Medical University endocrinology group, not by the Brawijaya authors PubMed lists.
entries.snippet: Department of Endocrinology and Metabolism, The Second Affiliated Hospital, Harbin Medical University

entries.proposition: IDENTITY: the DOI printed on the article is 10.18388/abp.2018_2632, volume 66, issue 2, pages 159-165; PubMed stores a different DOI and pages 679-686 for this PMID.
DESIGN: independent replication, in Han Chinese, of the ten loci from the East Asian meta-analysis; WWOX rs17797882 is one of ten tested index SNPs, not a hypothesis-driven WWOX study.
entries.snippet: 1 000 cases and 1 000 controls by the SNP scan method

entries.proposition: The WWOX variant enters as one of the ten East Asian GWAS index SNPs.
entries.snippet: were identified to be associated with T2DM

entries.proposition: CASES AND CONTROLS DIFFER in age (47 versus 42) and BMI (26.67 versus 23.14), the case controls being health-examination attendees; adjustment for age, sex and BMI is stated but the groups are not matched.
WWOX rs17797882 shows NO association with type 2 diabetes in this sample: risk allele frequency 0.245 in cases against 0.230 in controls, adjusted OR 1.054 (0.891-1.247), p 0.541.
The text places WWOX among the six SNPs not associated with T2D (only KCNK16 and GLIS3 are).
entries.snippet: were not associated with type 2 diabetes in the present

entries.proposition: The quantitative-trait analysis was run in the CONTROL group only, not in cases or the whole sample.
entries.snippet: Table 5. Association of 8 SNPs with quantitative traits related to glucose metabolism in controls.

entries.proposition: HOMA-beta effect of WWOX rs17797882 T allele: -29.231 with standard error 11.877, p 0.014; fasting glucose, HbA1c and HOMA-IR effects are null (p 0.309, 0.373, 0.918).
The text gives the same HOMA-beta coefficient with a different standard error (11.961), which in Table 5 belongs to the CMIP row; and gives TG beta 0.119 and HDL-C beta 0.037 with p 0.014 and 0.042.

Lipid traits in controls: WWOX rs17797882 T allele raises log triglycerides (beta 0.119, p 0.014) and HDL-cholesterol (beta 0.037, p 0.042); total and LDL cholesterol are null. Triglycerides and HDL-C moving up together is the opposite of the usual inverse pairing, and neither would survive a correction for about 64 trait tests.

The footnote states trait values were log-transformed before analysis, yet the HOMA-beta coefficients (-29.231, 8.521, 16.485) are on a raw-unit scale, unlike the fasting glucose coefficients (0.023, -0.045); the HOMA-beta effect size is therefore not interpretable as printed.
entries.snippet: bValues are log-transformed before the analysis

entries.proposition: The only significance rule stated is p below 0.05; no correction for the eight SNPs times eight traits (plus GRS) is described anywhere in the article text (searched by term: Bonferroni, multiple test, correct, FDR; zero hits).
entries.snippet: A p value < 0.05 was considered significant.

entries.proposition: The Discussion asserts the loci increased insulin resistance in the Chinese population; Table 5 shows no SNP and not the GRS associated with HOMA-IR (all p 0.347 or higher), so the sentence is not supported by the article's own table.
